chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed us of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abi Maryam, who said:

Ja'far عليه السلام narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام used to say: When a dog dies in the well, it is to be drained. And Ja'far عليه السلام said: If it falls into it and then is taken out of it alive, seven buckets are to be drawn from it.

His statement عليه السلام, 'When a dog dies in the well, it is to be drained,' is to be understood as referring to when one of the qualities of the water changes because of it, for that necessitates draining all of it. But if it does not change, then the ruling concerning it is what we have mentioned previously.

key_terms.أَوْصَافِ الْمَاءِ: the characteristics of the water, such as color, taste, or smell
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being evaluated for taharah and legal use
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling applicable to the case
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: the dog whose falling into or death in the well is the basis of the ruling
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets, the specified amount to be drawn when the dog is removed alive
key_terms.نُزِحَتْ: it is to be drained, meaning water is drawn out from the well
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرُ: it changes, referring to a perceptible change in the water's qualities

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dog falls into a well in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fiqh ruling concerning a dog falling into a well. It distinguishes between the case where the dog dies in the well and the case where it is removed alive, and it further clarifies that complete draining applies when the water's characteristics have changed.
